# Machine learning

Models small enough to train inside a box, in plain Kotlin, while you watch. Flow matching carries one 2D or 3D point cloud onto another and hands back the deformation between them; the multi-output regression head it trains is usable on its own. See [Flow Matching](../flow_matching.md).

## AgentEvalCorpus.kt { #agentevalcorpus-kt }

The agent eval corpus: tasks mined from the operation transcripts under `dev_docs/agents/transcripts/`
rather than written by hand.

[`InFieldAgentEvals`](machine-learning.md#infieldagentevals-kt-infieldagentevals) is seventeen tasks, so a pass rate over it moves 6% per task. The transcripts hold
about a thousand boxes that someone wrote and ran as real work, so each runnable one is a task:

- **goal**: make a box of this name, under these parents, that does what the box's own leading comment
  says, and whose output includes what the real box printed or displayed;
- **setup**: the box's ancestors in its transcript, created with their code and run in order;
- **solution**: the box's real code (`NewBoxRequest` + `RunBoxRequest`/`LaunchBoxRequest`), so every task
  carries a known-good answer to measure an agent against;
- **checks**: derived from what the solution said when run, twice: only output that came out the same
  both times becomes a check.

Mining is two stages. [`mine`](machine-learning.md#agentevalcorpus-kt--agentevalcorpus--mine) is static, YAML only, and rejects a box with a reason (never executed by its
transcript, needs a renderer / audio / the clock / files, prints nothing). Stage two runs each surviving
candidate's solution twice in a live Field and hands the pair to [`calibrate`](machine-learning.md#agentevalcorpus-kt--agentevalcorpus--calibrate), which either accepts it as a
[`CorpusTask`](machine-learning.md#agentevalcorpus-kt--agentevalcorpus--corpustask) or rejects it (`solution-fails`, `no-stable-output`). The calibrated corpus is checked in as
[`CHECKOUT_PATH`](machine-learning.md#agentevalcorpus-kt--agentevalcorpus--checkout-path), so an eval run does not re-mine.

The split is fixed by the task id ([`splitOf`](machine-learning.md#agentevalcorpus-kt--agentevalcorpus--splitof)): about a third of the tasks are `heldout`, never shown to
[`AgentLessons.distil`](machine-learning.md#agentlessons-kt--agentlessons--distil) when the protocol is followed (distil from a `train` run, measure on `heldout`).

## AgentTask.kt { #agenttask-kt }

Headless agent tasks: a goal, a document and a set of checks, run through AI4's own turn and judged from what the document's boxes did.

[`AgentTaskRequest`](machine-learning.md#agenttask-kt-agenttaskrequest) describes the task and its [`AgentCheck`](machine-learning.md#agenttask-kt-agentcheck)s, [`AgentTaskRunner`](machine-learning.md#agenttask-kt-agenttaskrunner) runs it, and
[`AgentTaskResult`](machine-learning.md#agenttask-kt-agenttaskresult) carries the verdict, each check's [`AgentCheckOutcome`](machine-learning.md#agenttask-kt-agentcheckoutcome) and the tool calls the agent
made ([`AgentToolCallRecord`](machine-learning.md#agenttask-kt-agenttoolcallrecord)).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/AgentTask.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/AgentTask/)

## AgentTaskTranscript.kt { #agenttasktranscript-kt }

Writes an agent task into a box's AI4 chat transcript, so a finished task can be read and continued in that box's chat panel.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/AgentTaskTranscript.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/AgentTaskTranscript/)

### AgentTaskTranscript { #agenttasktranscript-kt-agenttasktranscript }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">AgentTaskTranscript</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/AgentTaskTranscript/#L27)

Writes an agent task into a box's AI4 chat transcript (`ai4_chat_history`), in the transcript's own markup (`<<you>>`, `<<ai>>`, `<<progress>>`, `<<model:…>>`), and pushes it to the box's `ai-chat` panel. The panel then renders the task like any other turn, and the person can continue the conversation from there.

## BoxOutputCapture.kt { #boxoutputcapture-kt }

Pictures of a box's output area for the agent, taken from a headless Playwright page on the box's document, with simple statistics about what the picture contains.

[`BoxOutputCapture`](machine-learning.md#boxoutputcapture-kt-boxoutputcapture) owns the pages and their release; [`BoxOutputShot`](machine-learning.md#boxoutputcapture-kt-boxoutputshot) is one capture, and
[`PictureStats`](machine-learning.md#boxoutputcapture-kt-picturestats) summarises its pixels: how much differs from the background, and the dominant colours.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/BoxOutputCapture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/BoxOutputCapture/)

## FieldGraphTools.kt { #fieldgraphtools-kt }

The box graph and execution tools of Field's own agent: list, create, delete, edit, connect,
run, launch, stop and read the output of boxes in the current document.

These are the operations an external agent reaches through `tools/field_backdoor.py` (new-box,
set, connect, run, launch, stop, wait-output), registered as native tools in the AI4 registry.
Each one calls the same server function the websocket and backdoor handlers call
(`createAgentBox`, `executeAllRequest`, `launchAllRequest`, `stopBoxRequest`, and the action
table's `-connect`, `-disconnect` and `-delete-box`), so box execution is not reimplemented here.

A box that fails to compile or throws comes back as `success: false` with its diagnostics,
never as a silent success. [`FieldGraphHost`](machine-learning.md#fieldgraphtools-kt-fieldgraphhost) is how these tools reach the server:
[`LiveFieldGraphHost`](machine-learning.md#fieldgraphtools-kt-livefieldgraphhost) is the real one, and tests such as `InFieldAgentHarnessTest` supply a
scripted host.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/FieldGraphTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/FieldGraphTools/)

## GeometryReviewTools.kt { #geometryreviewtools-kt }

AI4 tools for the geometry review inbox: listing a document's Three.js and canvas review views, reading and answering their notes, reporting findings, styling parts and inspecting a view.

Each request class here is one tool, described to the model by its `@JsonClassDescription`; every
call returns a [`GeometryToolResult`](machine-learning.md#geometryreviewtools-kt-geometrytoolresult), which can attach saved pictures as images. The tools read and
write the same notes the viewer shows, scoped to the current document.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/)

**Used in:** [AI4's built-in tools](../ai4_tools.md), [Point to geometry, keep the context](../geometry_review.md)

### ListGeometryViewsRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-listgeometryviewsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ListGeometryViewsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">unused</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L35)

List the review views this document owns. This is where a `viewId` and the current `expectedRevision` come from, and the other tools here need both. Views belonging to other documents are not listed.

### StyleGeometryPartsRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-stylegeometrypartsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StyleGeometryPartsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">expectedRevision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">parts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">GeometryPartColor</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">unlit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">xrayOpacity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">replace</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L44)

Colour, highlight or ghost named parts of a solid viewer. The style map is stored on the source box, so it survives a rebuild that keeps the same part IDs; the geometry, the camera, the selection, the notes and the build's currency are all left alone.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--stylegeometrypartsrequest--parts"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">parts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">GeometryPartColor</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The parts to restyle, at most 10000, each named once and each present in the view as it stands. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--stylegeometrypartsrequest--unlit"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">unlit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Draw them at their own colour, with neither shading nor tone mapping. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--stylegeometrypartsrequest--xrayopacity"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">xrayOpacity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | How solid these parts stay while the rest fades, from 0 to 1, or null to follow the viewer's slider. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--stylegeometrypartsrequest--replace"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">replace</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Replace the view's whole style map rather than adding to it; an empty replacement restores defaults. |

### GeometryPartColor { #geometryreviewtools-kt-geometrypartcolor }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GeometryPartColor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">partId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L55)

One part's colour, as RGB from 0 to 1.

### ReadGeometryReviewsRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-readgeometryreviewsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReadGeometryReviewsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeResolved</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">offset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">limit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L65)

A page of a view's notes, as summaries rather than whole notes: id, kind, status and the revision each was made against. Reading leaves every status where it was. A note that came from a build attempt says whether that attempt ran against earlier inputs, in which case it may describe a design that is gone.

### ReadGeometryNoteRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-readgeometrynoterequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReadGeometryNoteRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">noteId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeImages</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L75)

One note whole: its text, the feature and view it points at, its replies and its resolution history, with the pictures saved when it was made attached as images. Those pictures are of the revision that was annotated, not of the geometry as it stands now; a picture whose bytes do not match its recorded hash is reported as a warning rather than attached.

### ReplyGeometryNoteRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-replygeometrynoterequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReplyGeometryNoteRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">noteId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">actor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">checkedRevision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">expectedVersion</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L84)

Add a reply to a note without closing it: what was checked, and against which revision. The note version from the latest read has to still be current, so two writers cannot answer the same note blind. [`ReviewGeometryNoteRequest`](machine-learning.md#geometryreviewtools-kt-reviewgeometrynoterequest) is the one that changes a note's status.

### ReviewGeometryNoteRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-reviewgeometrynoterequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReviewGeometryNoteRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">noteId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">status</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">summary</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">actor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">checkedRevision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">expectedVersion</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L93)

Resolve a note, or reopen one, with the revision the decision was checked against. The original note, its pictures, its replies and its history are kept either way. A note having been read, or the geometry having been rebuilt, is not a reason to resolve it.

### ReportGeometryFindingRequest { #geometryreviewtools-kt-reportgeometryfindingrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReportGeometryFindingRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">expectedRevision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stateJson</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">key</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stage</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">runId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">producer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">consequence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">prompt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L104)

Put a finding in front of a person, as a note in the same inbox their own annotations go to. It captures its own pictures in a separate viewer, so it never moves the camera the person is looking through, and it checks the revision again on the document thread: a capture that finished late cannot become a finding against newer geometry. Every field below is required, and two reports agreeing on `key`, `stage`, `runId` and `producer` are the same occurrence and reuse one thread.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--viewid"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">viewId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The view whose inbox the note goes to, from [`ListGeometryViewsRequest`](machine-learning.md#geometryreviewtools-kt-listgeometryviewsrequest). |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--expectedrevision"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">expectedRevision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The revision this finding is about, which has to still be the view's when the capture lands. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--statejson"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stateJson</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A complete state from [`InspectGeometryViewRequest`](machine-learning.md#geometryreviewtools-kt-inspectgeometryviewrequest), and one with a point or region selected. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--key"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">key</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What was checked and on what, as something stable across runs: `wall-thickness/lid`. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--kind"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | `error` for a failed check, `warning` for a suspected problem, `question` for a decision needed. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--stage"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stage</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The build stage the check belongs to. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--runid"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">runId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The build or diagnostic attempt it came from. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--producer"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">producer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What made the finding. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--text"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">text</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The finding itself, 1 to 16000 characters. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--consequence"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">consequence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What happens if it is left as it is, to 4000 characters. |
| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--reportgeometryfindingrequest--prompt"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">prompt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What is wanted back, to 4000 characters; a repair that needs no permission should say so. |

| <a id="geometryreviewtools-kt--inspectgeometryviewrequest--region"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">region</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">GeometryRegion</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | A rectangle to select, instead of a point. |

### GeometryPick { #geometryreviewtools-kt-geometrypick }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GeometryPick</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">y</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;face&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryReviewTools/#L175)

## GeometryViewCapture.kt { #geometryviewcapture-kt }

Independent viewer captures for the geometry review tools: a picture of a three.js view taken without
moving the one the user is looking at.

Each capture opens its own browser context on that view's page, applies the request's view state
(explode, hidden parts, x-ray, section plane, camera, picks and regions) through the page's inspector
API, waits for a frame to render, screenshots, and returns the image alongside the resulting state,
source list and part tree. The geometry's revision digest is read before and after, so a capture is
always of the revision the request named and a change in between is reported rather than photographed.
Captures collect in the box-output capture directory, where the hundred newest are kept.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/GeometryViewCapture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/GeometryViewCapture/)

## InFieldAgentEvals.kt { #infieldagentevals-kt }

A small eval suite for Field's own agent: seventeen tasks (five graded by pixels, three made of many similar calls
that a tool program does in one, two that are several turns of one conversation), each a goal, the setup it starts
from, checks that decide it, and a scripted solution.

The scripted solutions are real Kotlin for real Field. Replayed through [`ScriptedLlmBridge`](machine-learning.md#scriptedllmbridge-kt-scriptedllmbridge) against
a live Field (`agent-eval --mode scripted`) they test the tools, the execution path and the checkers
end to end with no model, and a scripted pass is the floor any model run should reach. Replayed in
jvmTest against a fake host, they test the harness logic. A `live` run hands the same goals and
checks to the configured provider and ignores the solutions.

Box names are fixed, so run each task in a fresh document ([`AgentEvalRunner`](machine-learning.md#infieldagentevals-kt-agentevalrunner) does).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/InFieldAgentEvals.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/InFieldAgentEvals/)

## KitTools.kt { #kittools-kt }

The AI4 tool that reports which kit a document runs and which of its kit-provided properties and assets have drifted from the kit.

[`InspectKitRequest`](machine-learning.md#kittools-kt-inspectkitrequest) is the tool and [`KitToolResult`](machine-learning.md#kittools-kt-kittoolresult) its answer. It reads only; migrating a
document to a newer kit is done by a person with `tools/field_kit.py`.

## StudyBuildTools.kt { #studybuildtools-kt }

AI4 tools over a box's study builds: list, inspect, start, wait for, cancel, await and prune build jobs.

Each request class is one tool and returns a [`StudyBuildToolResult`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-studybuildtoolresult). [`AwaitStudyBuildsRequest`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-awaitstudybuildsrequest)
is the exception: its [`StudyBuildAwaitResult`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-studybuildawaitresult) can end the turn with a suspension, which
[`StudyBuildAwaits`](machine-learning.md#studybuildawaits-kt-studybuildawaits) then holds until the jobs finish.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/)

**Used in:** [AI4's built-in tools](../ai4_tools.md), [Studies](../studies.md), [Let AI4 Wait for Long Builds](../ai4_long_builds.md)

### ListStudyBuildsRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-liststudybuildsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ListStudyBuildsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">unused</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L45)

List the document's build runners. This is where a `boxId` and `name` come from; every other tool here needs both, and a document with no runners answers with an empty list rather than a failure.

### InspectStudyBuildsRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-inspectstudybuildsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">InspectStudyBuildsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boxId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">offset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">limit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L54)

One runner's stages and a page of its attempt history, or one attempt named by `jobId`. Running, succeeded and current are three different things here: a stage's old success stops being current as soon as its inputs change. [`StartStudyBuildRequest`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-startstudybuildrequest) needs the stage fingerprint this reports.

### WaitStudyBuildRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-waitstudybuildrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">WaitStudyBuildRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boxId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">waitSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">600.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">afterUpdated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L63)

Watch a job that is already running, reporting its progress into the chat without spending a model turn on each poll. The wait ending is not the build failing: the result says whether the job is terminal. Cancelling the wait leaves the build running.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="studybuildtools-kt--waitstudybuildrequest--waitseconds"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">waitSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | How long to watch, 0 to 900 seconds. Reaching it ends the observation and not the build. |
| <a id="studybuildtools-kt--waitstudybuildrequest--afterupdated"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">afterUpdated</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A progress timestamp to return early on: the wait ends as soon as the job's own differs from it. |

### StartStudyBuildRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-startstudybuildrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StartStudyBuildRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boxId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stageId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">expectedFingerprint</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">waitSeconds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">JsonPropertyDescription</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;Optional parameters for this one attempt that the stage documents, as a JSON object in a string, such as a job to resume, e.g. &#96;{&#92;&quot;resume&#92;&quot;: &#92;&quot;&lt;jobId&gt;&#92;&quot;}&#96; or &#96;{&#92;&quot;budgetSeconds&#92;&quot;: 60}&#96;. Empty for none. Recorded in the attempt and part of its fingerprint; a later start does not reuse it, so pass it again when it still applies. Anything but a JSON object fails with success=false.&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">request</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L77)

Start one stage from the inputs it has now. The expected fingerprint comes from the latest [`InspectStudyBuildsRequest`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-inspectstudybuildsrequest), and a stage whose dependencies are missing or stale, whose gate is closed, or that is already building, is refused. A positive `waitSeconds` starts the job and watches it in the same call; zero returns the job handle for [`WaitStudyBuildRequest`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-waitstudybuildrequest) or [`AwaitStudyBuildsRequest`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-awaitstudybuildsrequest).

Anything that is not a JSON object fails the call. It goes into the attempt's fingerprint and is recorded with it, and it is not carried over, so a later start that still needs it passes it again. |

### CancelStudyBuildRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-cancelstudybuildrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CancelStudyBuildRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boxId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L94)

Ask a running build to stop. Success means the cancellation was recorded, not that the worker has stopped: it ends at its next cancellation check, so poll the same job until it is terminal. The stage keeps whatever result it had already published, and the attempt history survives.

### AwaitStudyBuildsRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-awaitstudybuildsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AwaitStudyBuildsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">boxId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jobIds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxHours</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">4.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L104)

End the turn and have Field wait for up to twenty jobs without the model, then start the conversation again with their outcomes. This is the alternative to repeated [`WaitStudyBuildRequest`](machine-learning.md#studybuildtools-kt-waitstudybuildrequest) calls for a build measured in hours: each wait costs a model round and this costs none. Jobs that have all already finished are answered at once and the turn carries on.

### PruneStudyBuildsRequest { #studybuildtools-kt-prunestudybuildsrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PruneStudyBuildsRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">JsonPropertyDescription</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;Job IDs to keep even when nothing else needs them, such as a result to compare against later.&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pins</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyList</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">@</span><span class="nc">JsonPropertyDescription</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">&quot;false (the default) reports what would be deleted and deletes nothing; true deletes it.&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">apply</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/agent/StudyBuildTools/#L114)

Delete attempt history nothing in this document still needs, across all of its runners. What is kept is each stage's current result, latest attempt and latest success, anything running, anything pinned, and whatever those were built from, gated on or resumed from. A deleted attempt cannot be inspected or resumed from again, so `apply` is false until asked for.

## AI4.kt { #ai4-kt }

Re-exports the AI4 assistant's public types and helpers under one package, `afield.ai.compat`, so
code that imports from this one package keeps compiling.

Every declaration here is a `typealias` or a one-line forwarding `val` or `fun` into the package
that now owns it: logging sinks from `afield.ai.diagnostics`, language specs such as
[`KOTLIN_SCRIPT`](workspace.md#languagespecs-kt--kotlin-script) and the GLSL and Slang stage specs from `afield.runtime.languages`, tool request
and result schemas from `afield.ai.tools`, and the completion helpers from `afield.ai.completion`.
New code should import from those packages directly.

The file also declares two `@RunsAt(installHandlers)` hooks, [`ai4_install`](machine-learning.md#ai4-kt--ai4-install) and
[`docs_search_install`](machine-learning.md#ai4-kt--docs-search-install), which call `installAi4` and `installDocsSearch` (the latter installs the
`docs_search_input` message handler).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/compat/AI4.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/compat/AI4/)

## Ai4CompletionDoc.kt { #ai4completiondoc-kt }

Drafts documentation, with a language model, for a completion item whose declaration has no KDoc.

[`Ai4CompletionDoc.resolveDoc`](machine-learning.md#ai4completiondoc-kt--ai4completiondoc--resolvedoc) finds the item's definition through the Kotlin source index and
returns nothing when that definition already carries a KDoc. Otherwise it sends the declaration's
source to a fast model and caches the draft in [`GENERATED_COMPLETION_DOCS_FILE`](machine-learning.md#ai4completiondoc-kt--generated-completion-docs-file), keyed by symbol,
file, line and a hash of the declaration source, so an edited declaration gets a fresh draft.
[`Ai4CompletionDoc.dropStaleGeneratedDocs`](machine-learning.md#ai4completiondoc-kt--ai4completiondoc--dropstalegenerateddocs) evicts drafts whose source has changed or gone; it is
covered by `GeneratedCompletionDocSweepTest`. Drafts the docs revision pass declined, listed in
[`GENERATED_COMPLETION_DOCS_DECLINED_FILE`](machine-learning.md#ai4completiondoc-kt--generated-completion-docs-declined-file), are neither shown nor regenerated.

The model is `AFIELD_COMPLETION_DOC_MODEL`, defaulting to the fast model.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/completion/Ai4CompletionDoc.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/completion/Ai4CompletionDoc/)

## Ai4GlslAutocomplete.kt { #ai4glslautocomplete-kt }

Language-model autocomplete for shader properties (`fragment`, `vertex`, `compute` and the other
shader stages).

[`Ai4GlslAutocomplete.complete`](machine-learning.md#ai4glslautocomplete-kt--ai4glslautocomplete--complete) marks the cursor in the box's shader code, wraps it for the stage's
language, adds context from the shader include library, and asks a fast model for three
candidates, each with a one-line note. It returns them as [`CompletionCandidate`](machine-learning.md#ai4glslautocomplete-kt-completioncandidate)s. One model thread
is kept per file key, so later requests in the same editor reuse the conversation.

The model is `AFIELD_SHADER_AUTOCOMPLETE_MODEL` (or `AFIELD_GLSL_AUTOCOMPLETE_MODEL`), defaulting
to the fast model.

## AiChatFenceCatalog.kt { #aichatfencecatalog-kt }

The fenced blocks AI4 chat draws as pictures rather than printing as code, read on the JVM from
the same catalog the browser renderers read.

`src/commonMain/resources/ai4-fence-renderers.json` holds one entry per language, each naming the
renderer module and export that draws it in the chat panel alongside the syntax guidance and the
worked example the model is shown. There are two today, `mermaid` and `math`. The JVM reads that
file out of its resources and turns it into the paragraph of fence instructions added to the
chat system prompt, so a language the model is told about always has a renderer behind it and a
language the browser cannot draw is never offered. Only chat mode gets that paragraph; the other
instruction modes describe no fences.

The catalog is checked on first read for a known schema version, one entry per language, a
lowercase language name and no blank field. A malformed or absent catalog stops the read and says
what is wrong with it, instead of leaving the panel one renderer short of what it advertised.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiChatFenceCatalog.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiChatFenceCatalog/)

## AiLiveConversation.kt { #ailiveconversation-kt }

The running transcript of one AI4 chat turn, assembled in the order things happened.

A turn interleaves three kinds of entry: text streamed from the model, the activity lines that
say which tool is running, and anything the person typed while the turn was still going. Each is
appended as it arrives, and the whole sequence renders into the `<<ai>>`, `<<you>>` and
`<<progress>>` markers that a box's `ai4_chat_history` property stores and `aiChatHistoryHtml`
turns into the chat panel.

Two rules keep that order readable while the turn is live. Consecutive text deltas merge into one
block instead of one block per delta, and a new activity line replaces the previous one only
where that one was still transient, so a finished tool's result or failure is never overwritten
by the next thing to start. The newest activity line of a live turn is marked `<<progress-open>>`
and renders expanded; the earlier ones stay collapsed.

At the end the bridge hands back the turn's final text, which usually repeats what was already
streamed. Rendering drops the streamed copy when the final text starts with it and nothing but
completion activity follows it, so the reader is left with one answer rather than two.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiLiveConversation.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiLiveConversation/)

## AiRequestLedger.kt { #airequestledger-kt }

The on-disk accounting record for every AI4 model request: which endpoint answered, how many
tokens it billed, how long it took and how it ended, with none of the prompt and none of the
reply.

The OpenAI Responses bridge and the Anthropic messages bridge both write through it, so a
session's whole model spend lands in one place whatever provider served it. Lines are appended as
JSON under `~/.afield/logs/ai_usage`, redirected by the `afield.ai.usageLog.path` system property
or the `AFIELD_AI_USAGE_LOG_PATH` environment variable. A file name carries the date, the process
id and a uuid minted per JVM, so two Field processes logging at once never share a file or
contend for a lock.

Four events describe one request. `attempt_started` opens each attempt; `response_usage` records
the billed token counts, normalised so that input means the whole prompt for either provider and
cached input is part of it; `retry_wait` marks a backoff between attempts; and
`attempt_finished` carries the elapsed time, the error type, the HTTP status and whichever
rate-limit headers the provider returned. Usage is recorded before the response is validated,
because a stream that failed partway can still have billed.

Writing is best effort. A directory that cannot be written prints one warning to stderr and the
request carries on, since losing accounting is not a reason to lose the answer.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiRequestLedger.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiRequestLedger/)

### FieldBuildInfo { #aisessiontree-kt-fieldbuildinfo }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">FieldBuildInfo</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiSessionTree/#L564)

Which Field this is: the checkout's commit, whether the tree was dirty, and a hash of the diff — what a capability checkpoint records so a transcript says which code its tools ran on. Read once, in the background, from `git` in the working directory (a packaged build may ship `field-build-info.properties` instead, which wins). Not a Gradle-generated resource: one that changes on every commit would make every test task out of date.

## AiStatePruning.kt { #aistatepruning-kt }

Housekeeping for the box states AI4 conversations save under `<document>/ai4_blobs/state/`.

[`AiStatePruning.sweepOrphans`](machine-learning.md#aistatepruning-kt--aistatepruning--sweeporphans) removes states no session tree refers to, and [`Box.pruneAiStates`](machine-learning.md#aistatepruning-kt--pruneaistates)
trims old states along each branch on request, reporting by default rather than deleting.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiStatePruning.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiStatePruning/)

### Top-level functions { #aistatepruning-kt-functions }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="aistatepruning-kt--pruneaistates"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">pruneAiStates</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">keepPerBranch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">dryRun</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AiStatePruning</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Report</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiStatePruning/#L104) | Free disk taken by this document's saved AI4 box states, keeping the latest `keepPerBranch` along every branch of every conversation and the state at every fork. A turn whose state is removed can still be rewound to, but its box is not restored. Reports what it would remove unless `dryRun` is false. |

## AiToastPolicy.kt { #aitoastpolicy-kt }

Which AI4 log lines become a toast on the canvas, and which stay in the log.

A turn logs a great deal, and almost none of it is addressed to the person watching. Only events
carrying the `ai.user` channel are candidates, which is what `userNotice` writes; everything else
a bridge or a tool logs is diagnostics, and the log viewer is where it belongs.

Candidates are then thinned twice. The same text repeated inside fifteen seconds is dropped, and
an ordinary notice arriving within five seconds of the last one is dropped as well, so a burst of
activity shows one line rather than six. A notice also carrying `warning` or `error` skips the
five-second gate and is held back only by the repeat test.

`toolActivity` is the other half of the policy. It maps a handful of tool names to one short
phrase each, "Checking the view…" or "Updating the document…", and says nothing for the rest:
reads, discovery and unfamiliar tools are already visible in the chat panel and the tool pool,
and a tool's implementation name is not a description of what was asked for.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiToastPolicy.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiToastPolicy/)

## AiToolFailure.kt { #aitoolfailure-kt }

What a chat turn does when a tool throws. Three answers live here: which failures end the turn rather
than becoming the call's output, what the model reads in place of a result, and what is written back
for a call the turn ended before answering.

The provider's thread has to hold an output for every call it made, so a turn that stops mid-round
still writes one for each call left outstanding; without it, every later turn in that chat is refused
for a function call with no output.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiToolFailure.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiToolFailure/)

## AiTurnCancellation.kt { #aiturncancellation-kt }

Telling a stopped AI4 turn apart from one that failed.

Stopping a turn arrives as a `CancellationException` or an `InterruptedException`, but rarely at
the top of the throwable: a future, a coroutine or a reflective tool call wraps it, sometimes
several layers down, so the type that was thrown says nothing by itself. The one function here
walks the cause chain for either of those two, guarding against a cycle on the way.

It is asked wherever the agent loop would otherwise swallow an exception and carry on. Saving and
restoring a conversation's branch state both do that, and both rethrow instead when this answers
yes, so a turn the person stopped is not written into the transcript as a step that failed.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiTurnCancellation.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiTurnCancellation/)

The bridge hands waiting messages to the model at the next tool-round boundary, and whatever is left

## AiWorldUndo.kt { #aiworldundo-kt }

Which boxes an abandoned turn created can be deleted without taking anyone's later work with them.

The world undo after a rewind (`ai-chat-rewind-world`) undoes the abandoned turns' property edits strictly
(an edit changed since is skipped) and deletes the boxes they created. A person may since have typed into
one of those boxes, moved it, or wired it to their own; the panel promises that anything changed since is
left alone. So every turn records a fingerprint of each box its conversation has created, as the turn
starts and as it ends (`AiSessionTree.TurnMeta.createdBefore` / `createdAfter`), and a box is deleted only
when it is exactly as the last abandoned turn left it, and nobody changed it between abandoned turns either.

A fingerprint covers the box's name, frame, links to other boxes and every property that is saved with the
document, apart from the chat's own (`ai4_*`). Values are written out typed and quoted, lists in their own
order (their order can be a polygon's vertices or an authored sequence) and only sets and maps sorted, so
two different values never print alike. The one normalisation is for `LOADER_DEFAULTS`, properties that
loading a document fills in when absent, so an untouched box still matches its own fingerprint after its
document is reopened.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/AiWorldUndo.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/AiWorldUndo/)

## ContextPipeline.kt { #contextpipeline-kt }

The parts an AI4 turn's prompt is built from, tagged with how long each is kept and whether it changes between turns.

A [`TurnContext`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt-turncontext) holds a turn's [`ContextFragment`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt-contextfragment)s and the request that follows them; each fragment
carries a [`FragmentRetention`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt-fragmentretention) (stored with the message, or sent for this turn only) and a [`Stability`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt-stability)
(cacheable across turns, or not). The provider bridges decide where each kind goes, and
[`TurnContext.legacyPrompt`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt--turncontext--legacyprompt) rebuilds the single-string prompt for bridges that send one.
[`ContextReport`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt-contextreport) is what `/context` shows about a turn, and [`ContextPipeline.enabledByDefault`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt--contextpipeline--enabledbydefault) reads the
`afield.ai4.ephemeralInstructions` switch.

### Kept { #contextpipeline-kt-kept }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Kept</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/ContextPipeline/#L157)

Where a fragment ends up, given where the bridge put it ([`ContextReport.placement`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt--contextreport--placement)). The fragment classes describe intent; the provider decides retention, and these differ: OpenAI's conversations live on its side, so anything sent inside one stays there.

Constants: `EVERY_TURN`, `ONCE`, `STORED`, `EVERY_REQUEST`, `THIS_TURN`.

## IdeChatHelpers.kt { #idechathelpers-kt }

The entry points an editor or chat panel calls to run one AI4 turn against a box's code.

[`IdeChatHelpers`](machine-learning.md#idechathelpers-kt-idechathelpers) wraps an [`LlmBridge`](machine-learning.md#llmbridge-kt-llmbridge). [`IdeChatHelpers.chatFile`](machine-learning.md#idechathelpers-kt--idechathelpers--chatfile), [`IdeChatHelpers.chatInline`](machine-learning.md#idechathelpers-kt--idechathelpers--chatinline) and
[`IdeChatHelpers.chatError`](machine-learning.md#idechathelpers-kt--idechathelpers--chaterror) build the turn's instructions and tool context, run it through the bridge,
and return an [`IdeChatHelpers.HighLevelResult`](machine-learning.md#idechathelpers-kt--idechathelpers--highlevelresult) with the edited code, commentary and tool transcript;
[`IdeChatHelpers.chatGeneral`](machine-learning.md#idechathelpers-kt--idechathelpers--chatgeneral) runs a chat turn and returns the bridge's own result.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/IdeChatHelpers.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/IdeChatHelpers/)

## Instructions.kt { #instructions-kt }

The instruction text AI4 sends the model with each turn, per kind of turn.

[`InstructionMode`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt-instructionmode) names the kinds (general, inline, error, chat). [`buildInstructionFragments`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt--buildinstructionfragments) assembles
a turn's instructions as [`ContextFragment`](machine-learning.md#contextpipeline-kt-contextfragment)s from the base contract, the tool guidance and the document's
context, and [`buildDynamicInstructions`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt--builddynamicinstructions) joins them into one string. [`generalInstructions`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt--generalinstructions),
[`inlineInstructions`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt--inlineinstructions), [`errorInstructions`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt--errorinstructions) and [`generalChatInstructions`](machine-learning.md#instructions-kt--generalchatinstructions) are the per-mode texts.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/Instructions.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/Instructions/)

## TurnSuspension.kt { #turnsuspension-kt }

How a tool result ends a model's turn early so the conversation can wait for study builds without spending model calls.

A tool result implementing [`SuspendsTurn`](machine-learning.md#turnsuspension-kt-suspendsturn) carries a [`TurnSuspension`](machine-learning.md#turnsuspension-kt-turnsuspension): the [`AwaitedBuild`](machine-learning.md#turnsuspension-kt-awaitedbuild) jobs and a
deadline. The bridge stops after the current round and keeps that round's tool outputs as a
[`SuspendedRound`](machine-learning.md#turnsuspension-kt-suspendedround), which the resuming turn sends ahead of its own prompt.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/TurnSuspension.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/TurnSuspension/)

### SuspendsTurn { #turnsuspension-kt-suspendsturn }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">SuspendsTurn</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/TurnSuspension/#L22)

A tool result that ends the model's turn when [`suspension`](machine-learning.md#turnsuspension-kt--suspendsturn--suspension) is set: the bridge finishes the round it is in, makes no further model request, and returns the suspension in [`OpenAiIdeCodexBridge.SendResult`](machine-learning.md#openaiidecodexbridge-kt--openaiidecodexbridge--sendresult). Someone else resumes the conversation later (`StudyBuildAwaits` for `AwaitStudyBuildsRequest`), so the time spent waiting costs no model calls.

## ChatArchive.kt { #chatarchive-kt }

### The chat archive: a saved AI4 conversation, read from disk as a tree

An AI4 chat is saved as two box properties (`AiBoxConversation`, `AiSessionTree`):
- `ai4_chat_history`, the transcript the panel shows: the current branch only, images inline.
- `ai4_session`, the session tree: every turn as a node with a parent, including turns rewound away, with
  a timestamp, the model, token usage and images as `ai4img:` references into `<document>/ai4_blobs/`.

This reads both from a document folder without opening the document. No Field server or box is involved,
so it is safe to point at a document someone is working in. The tree is the source, and the transcript is
used to check it: transcript text past the tree's head (a verdict appended by an agent task, an
interrupted turn) becomes an `unrecorded` node, and a transcript that no longer starts with the head (a
hand edit) becomes an `unrecorded` root. That is what `AiSessionTree` would record the next time it reconciles the box.

#### Addresses

Every block has an address, `<nodeId>.b<index>`: the session-tree node that added it, and its position in
that node's markdown. Node ids are written once and never reused, so an address stays valid as the chat
grows, and a block in an abandoned branch has one just as a block on the current branch does. Summaries
written over a chat (lenses) cite these addresses.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/chatlog/ChatArchive.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/chatlog/ChatArchive/)

## ChatArchiveCli.kt { #chatarchivecli-kt }

### Chat archive statistics from the command line

[`ChatArchiveCli`](machine-learning.md#chatarchivecli-kt-chatarchivecli) reads saved AI4 chats from document folders through [`ChatArchive`](machine-learning.md#chatarchive-kt-chatarchive) and prints a [`ChatStats`](machine-learning.md#chatarchivecli-kt-chatstats)
row per chat (shape, tool calls by family, images, tokens), as a table or JSON, or prints the outline and read
views an agent would see ([`ChatLogViews`](machine-learning.md#chatlogviews-kt-chatlogviews)). It never opens a document in Field.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/chatlog/ChatArchiveCli.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/chatlog/ChatArchiveCli/)

## ChatLensViewer.kt { #chatlensviewer-kt }

### The lens viewer

A lens beside the chat it summarizes, both drawn by the chat panel's renderer, with a band from each lens
block to the stretch of the chat it stands for (`chatLens.js`). A box shows one with
```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
showChatLens("house-machine-10", "storyline")
```
in a box whose document has run [`registerChatlogTools`](machine-learning.md#chatlogtools-kt--registerchatlogtools): the viewer reads chats and lenses through that
document's [`ChatlogStore`](machine-learning.md#chatlogtools-kt-chatlogstore), over the routes in `ChatlogRoutes.kt`, which answer only for documents that
registered one.

## ChatLogViews.kt { #chatlogviews-kt }

### What an agent reads of a chat

Text views of a [`ChatTree`](machine-learning.md#chatarchive-kt-chattree) for AI4 agents that write lenses ([`registerChatlogTools`](machine-learning.md#chatlogtools-kt--registerchatlogtools)). Every view names blocks by
address, so what the agent reads is what it cites. Tool activity reads as round lines in the panel's own
words (`AiChatRound`); images read as their captions and `ai4img:` references, never as bytes.

## ChatlogTools.kt { #chatlogtools-kt }

### Chat-log tools: AI4 agents that read chats and write lenses

A box hands its document's AI4 agents a chat archive by running, once:
```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
registerChatlogTools(File("/path/to/workspace"))
```
Agents then see `chatlog.list`, `chatlog.outline`, `chatlog.read`, `chatlog.search`, `chatlog.images` and
`lens.write`, `lens.read`, `lens.list`. The archive is only read (see [`ChatArchive`](machine-learning.md#chatarchive-kt-chatarchive)); the chats can live in
another workspace, including one a person is working in.

A **lens** is a shorter chat written over a longer one: the same `<<you>>`/`<<ai>>` markup, so the chat panel
renders it, with a `<<source:a..b>>` line at the top of each block saying which stretch of the chat it
stands for. Lenses are saved in `lensDir`, by default this document's `lenses/` folder, as
`<chat>/<name>.md` beside a `<name>.json` record of the brief that made it.

Chats are named `<document>` when the document has one chat, otherwise `<document>/<box name or id>`. A lens is
itself a chat, named `<chat>#<lens>`: the tools outline, read and cite it like any other, so a lens can be written
over a lens (`house-machine-10#episodes`), and the viewer shows the whole chain.

A **series** runs several chats end to end, as one chat: `series:<glob>` takes every chat whose name matches
(`series:house-machine-*`), and `series:<glob>@<lens>` takes each one's lens of that name instead, skipping chats
that have none. A series is outlined, read and cited like a chat (its addresses are its chats' own), so a lens
over a series (`series:house-machine-*@storyline#arc`) tells the story across them.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/conversation/chatlog/ChatlogTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/conversation/chatlog/ChatlogTools/)

## Logging.kt { #logging-kt }

The channel-tagged log events the AI tooling writes, and the sinks that receive them.

A [`LogEvent`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-logevent) carries a channel (a comma-separated set of tags such as `info,ai.toolio`), a
message, and optional block indent and boundary markers. [`LogDispatcher`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-logdispatcher) fans each event out to
every installed [`LogSink`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-logsink); [`LogDispatcher.withSink`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt--withsink) attaches one for the length of a block.

### Sinks

- [`StdoutLog`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-stdoutlog) — prints to the terminal, skipping channels muted by [`ConsoleMute`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-consolemute).
- [`NotifyLog`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-notifylog) — prints like [`StdoutLog`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-stdoutlog) and also raises a clipped, de-duplicated toast.
- [`SilentLog`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-silentlog) — drops everything.

[`ChannelMatch`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-channelmatch) is the rule all channel selectors share: a selector matches when each of its tags
is among the channel's.

### File traces

[`TraceLogger`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-tracelogger) appends sectioned, truncated text to a trace file when `afield.ai4.trace` (or
`AFIELD_AI4_TRACE`) is set; `1`/`true` selects `~/.afield/logs/ai4_trace.log`. [`AiToolIoLogger`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-aitooliologger)
writes one JSONL file per tool session under `~/.afield/logs/ai4_tool_io`, on unless
`afield.ai4.toolIoLog` (or `AFIELD_AI4_TOOL_IO_LOG`) is `0`, `false` or `off`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/diagnostics/Logging.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/diagnostics/Logging/)

**Used in:** [Logging: channels, sinks and the console](../logging.md), [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md), [Agent transcript gallery](../agent_transcripts.md)

### ChannelMatch { #logging-kt-channelmatch }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ChannelMatch</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/diagnostics/Logging/#L143)

The one rule every channel selector follows — the console mute set, the pinned console and the `LogStream` filter: a channel is a comma-separated set of tags, and a selector matches when every one of its tags is among the channel's. So `boxes` matches `info,boxes` and `boxes,debug`; `info,boxes` matches `boxes,info` and `info,boxes,slow`; `kotlin` does not match `kotlinjs`. Tags compare exactly, case included, as written at the call site.

### ConsoleMute { #logging-kt-consolemute }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ConsoleMute</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/diagnostics/Logging/#L162)

Channels suppressed from the console — both the plain [`StdoutLog`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-stdoutlog) and the interactive PinnedConsole honor this. Muted events still reach every *other* sink (e.g. the LogStream web widget), so nothing is lost; they're just too chatty for the terminal. Default mutes the chatty background channels (`info,boxes`, `info,persist`, `info,ai.boxnames`, `debug,boxes`). Override with `-Dafield.log.mute=...` or `AFIELD_LOG_MUTE=...` (semicolon-separated selectors, matched by [`ChannelMatch`](machine-learning.md#logging-kt-channelmatch): `boxes` mutes every channel tagged `boxes`); set to a blank/empty value to mute nothing.

## Clip.kt { #clip-kt }

CLIP, as a source of *directions in meaning*.

[CLIP](https://openai.com/research/clip) embeds images and text into one 512-dimensional space. Two
separate ONNX graphs — `text_model.onnx` and `vision_model.onnx` — each emit an already-projected
512-vector, so no head has to be reimplemented here.

That gives three uses:

 1. **Zero-shot classification with no training.** Encode a handful of prompts once, cosine them
    against the live frame, take the best. See [`ClipVector.classify`](machine-learning.md#clip-kt--clipvector--classify).
 2. **Identity by similarity.** A stored vector plus a threshold is a recogniser.
 3. **A knob whose units are meaning.** `clipEncode("storm") - clipEncode("calm")` is a *direction*, and
    projecting the current frame onto it is a continuous parameter that tracks a semantic axis
    rather than a pixel statistic. See [`ClipVector.axisTo`](machine-learning.md#clip-kt--clipvector--axisto).

Encode prompts once, into a `val`, and the text tower stays out of the per-frame path.

### Cosine values are not comparable across modalities

This is why [`ClipVector.classify`](machine-learning.md#clip-kt--clipvector--classify) ranks prompts rather than thresholding a bare cosine. Measured on this checkpoint:

 * **text against text** sits in a narrow high cone — `cos("storm","calm") = 0.881`,
   `cos("a photo of a cat","a photo of a dog") = 0.931`. Nothing is ever near 0.
 * **image against text** sits far lower — around `0.21` for every prompt tried, because the two
   towers occupy offset regions of the sphere (the "modality gap").

So `0.21` does not mean "unrelated" and `0.88` does not mean "the same". Only *rank* and
*difference* carry information: compare one image against several prompts, or track how a
projection moves over time. An absolute threshold on a raw cosine does not transfer between prompts or scenes.

### Cost

Text is ≈5ms per prompt, after the one-off cost of loading the encoder. Vision is ≈36ms at
224x224 on a CPU provider, far cheaper than [`DepthAnything`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt-depthanything), but still not free, so drive it from a worker if it is per-frame.

The text tower is [`ClipText`](machine-learning.md#clip-kt-cliptext) and the vision tower is [`ClipImage`](machine-learning.md#clip-kt-clipimage).

## DepthAnything.kt { #depthanything-kt }

Monocular depth, from any image, with no depth camera.

[Depth Anything V2](https://depth-anything-v2.github.io) Small is the least demanding useful vision
model there is: one image in, one single-channel map out, no anchors, no non-maximum suppression,
no decode step and no state between frames, so what it exercises is the ONNX plumbing that harder
models reuse.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val depth = DepthAnything(width = 266, height = 266)
depth.infer(webcamRgbaBuffer, srcW = 640, srcH = 480)
// depth.depthFp16 now holds width*height fp16 values in [0,1]
```

### The output is inverse relative depth, in arbitrary units

`predicted_depth` is not
metres and not normalised. On the synthetic frame [`OnnxSmokeTest`](machine-learning.md#onnxsmoketest-kt-onnxsmoketest) uses, the raw range at 518x518 is
`[1.0353, 2.8187]` and at 266x266 it is `[1.2826, 1.9854]` — both asserted there against a Python
`onnxruntime` reference. The range moves
with the *content and the resolution*, and **larger means nearer**.

So a usable texture needs a normalisation window, and choosing it per-frame from that frame's own
min and max makes the image flicker: a hand entering shot rescales the entire background.
[`DepthAnything`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt-depthanything) instead tracks the window with an exponential moving average
([`DepthAnything.adaptation`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--adaptation)) and normalises
against the smoothed window, which is the cheap version of the one-euro filter that anything
body-tracked eventually needs. [`DepthStats`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt-depthstats) reports both the raw and the smoothed window so a box
can watch that decision rather than guess at it.

### Buffers keep their identity

[`DepthAnything.depthFp16`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--depthfp16) and [`DepthAnything.depthRaw`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--depthraw) are allocated once and refilled in place. That is not just to avoid
garbage: `afield.graphics.texture.StreamingTexture` captures its source buffer at *construction* and
re-reads it every frame, so the buffer has to keep the same identity for the texture to keep
working. Uploading to Vulkan is then:

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val tex = StreamingTexture(
    depth.depthFp16, depth.width, depth.height,
    imageFormat = VK10.VK_FORMAT_R16_SFLOAT
)
```

fp16 is the output format because a single-channel depth map has nowhere near 16 bits of real
precision in it, and `R16_SFLOAT` halves the upload against `R32_SFLOAT` for no visible loss.

### Cost

Inference is **not** frame-rate on a CPU execution provider: ≈388ms at 518x518 and ≈101ms at
266x266 on a 10-core Apple Silicon machine, and see [`OnnxRuntime`](machine-learning.md#onnxruntime-kt-onnxruntime) for why CoreML does not fix that.
Cost is roughly quadratic in resolution, which makes [`DepthAnything.width`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--width) and [`DepthAnything.height`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--height)
the main lever. Anything interactive should drive this through [`DepthAnythingWorker`](machine-learning.md#depthanythingworker-kt-depthanythingworker) rather than calling
[`DepthAnything.infer`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--infer) on the render thread.

## DepthAnythingWorker.kt { #depthanythingworker-kt }

[`DepthAnything`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt-depthanything) on its own thread, so a 100–400ms inference cannot stall the renderer.

Depth Anything Small costs ≈101ms at 266x266 and ≈388ms at 518x518 on a CPU execution provider; calling
[`DepthAnything.infer`](machine-learning.md#depthanything-kt--depthanything--infer) from a render loop turns 60fps into 2.6fps. So the renderer gets *staleness* instead of
latency: the most recent depth map that happens to be finished, which at 266x266 is six frames old at 60fps and looks
fine for displacement, parallax and depth-keyed compositing, and looks like lag for anything a hand is steering
directly.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
// once
val depth = DepthAnythingWorker(width = 266, height = 266)
val tex = StreamingTexture(depth.depthFp16, depth.width, depth.height,
                           imageFormat = VK10.VK_FORMAT_R16_SFLOAT)
// per frame
depth.submit(webcam.frameBuffer, 640, 480)   // returns immediately, drops old frames
if (depth.consume()) tex.recordUpload(commandBuffer)
```

### Frames are dropped, not queued

[`DepthAnythingWorker.submit`](machine-learning.md#depthanythingworker-kt--depthanythingworker--submit) overwrites any frame that has not been picked up yet. A queue would be wrong here: it
would grow without bound whenever inference is slower than capture, which is always, and every frame it held would be
more stale than the one behind it. Dropping means the model is always working on the newest frame available when it
became free.

### Why consume copies

[`DepthAnythingWorker.depthFp16`](machine-learning.md#depthanythingworker-kt--depthanythingworker--depthfp16) has a fixed identity because `StreamingTexture` captures its source buffer once, at
construction. The worker therefore cannot write into it directly — the renderer could be reading it mid-write and
would show a torn map with a visible seam. Instead the worker publishes into an internal buffer, and
[`DepthAnythingWorker.consume`](machine-learning.md#depthanythingworker-kt--depthanythingworker--consume) copies that into [`DepthAnythingWorker.depthFp16`](machine-learning.md#depthanythingworker-kt--depthanythingworker--depthfp16) under the lock, on the calling thread.
The copy is ~537KB at 518x518, tens of microseconds, and it is the only work the render thread does.

## Lpips.kt { #lpips-kt }

LPIPS: how different two pictures look, as a learned perceptual distance.

`0` is identical, and larger is more different; for natural images most distances fall between 0
and about 0.8. It is Zhang et al.'s "Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity" (CVPR 2018,
[richzhang/PerceptualSimilarity](https://github.com/richzhang/PerceptualSimilarity), BSD-2),
version 0.1 with the AlexNet backbone: both images go through AlexNet's five convolution stages,
each stage's activations are normalised per position, and the squared differences are weighted
by a linear layer trained on human judgements of which of two distortions looks closer to the
original. So it compares edges, blobs and textures where they are, not pixel colours.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val d = Lpips.distance(imgFromFile("a.png"), imgFromFile("b.png"))
val ds = Lpips.distances(candidates, target)   // many against one, the target computed once
```

Both images must be the same size, at least 32 pixels on each side, RGB or grey in `0..1`.

### Size matters

AlexNet's first stage has stride 4 and the network halves twice more, so at 32x32 the three
deepest stages are 1x1: they still see the image, but only as a whole. Measured on fixed
pairs (see `tools/export_lpips_onnx.py`), a yellow disc against a colour ramp is 0.42 at 32
pixels, 0.68 at 64 and 0.83 at 128; the same pair, the same verdict, a compressed scale.
Compare distances made at one size with each other, not across sizes.

### Where the model comes from

Field exports its own AlexNet LPIPS ONNX file: `tools/export_lpips_onnx.py` builds it from the `lpips` package on PyPI (0.1.4, which ships
the trained linear weights) and torchvision's ImageNet AlexNet, checks the ONNX graph against the
PyTorch module (agreement 1.2e-7 on twelve pairs), and installs a 9.9MB file in the
[`OnnxModel`](machine-learning.md#onnxruntime-kt-onnxmodel) cache. [`Lpips.ensureModel`](machine-learning.md#lpips-kt--lpips--ensuremodel) runs that script through `uv` the first time it is needed — a
one-off of about a minute that downloads PyTorch if `uv` has not cached it — and checks the result
against [`Lpips.MODEL`](machine-learning.md#lpips-kt--lpips--model)'s pinned sha256, which two exports with the pinned package versions reproduced
byte for byte.

### Its gradient

[`Lpips.distanceAndGradientPlanar`](machine-learning.md#lpips-kt--lpips--distanceandgradientplanar) also returns d distance / d candidate pixel, from a second exported
graph ([`Lpips.GRAD_MODEL`](machine-learning.md#lpips-kt--lpips--grad-model)) that the same script builds and checks against PyTorch's autograd. That is
what lets a fit descend on LPIPS: `afield.lang.stacksl.cpu.StackSLFit` seeds its per-pixel tapes with
it.
